_meta.purpose: Category-level periodicity priors for agents/periodicity_inference.py. This file IS the methodology for Section 3's step-3 'category prior' signal, in the same way data/banking77_bucket_map.json is the methodology for the intent taxonomy: the values are visible, versioned, dated and attributed rather than being an undocumented dict inside a module.
_meta.honest_limitation: Every entry below with source='illustrative_default' is exactly that — a plausible modal period chosen to make the clarifying question read naturally, NOT a figure derived from any dataset. No public dataset of retail payment periodicity by expense category was available for this project, and inventing an empirical-looking citation for a number that has no dataset behind it would be a worse failure than saying so. A deploying institution is expected to replace these with priors fitted to its own transaction population — see how_to_override.
_meta.how_to_override: Point settings.budget.periodicity_priors_path at a different JSON file with the same schema, or edit this one. No code change is needed. agents.periodicity_inference falls back to _BUILTIN_PRIORS if the file is missing or malformed, so a bad override degrades to the documented defaults rather than crashing a customer session.
_meta.invariant: A prior may only affect the PHRASING of a clarifying question (its 'most customers pay this X' hint) and the ranking of candidate questions. It may never cause a question to be skipped, and it may never be written into monthly_expenses as though it were observed. Enforced by test_periodicity_inference.TestPriorsAreAdvisoryOnly.

field_definitions.ambiguous: Whether a single observed occurrence of this category is genuinely ambiguous enough to be worth asking about (given materiality). Categories not listed here at all are treated as non-ambiguous.
field_definitions.modal_period: The most common period for this category, used ONLY as a phrasing hint. null means 'no defensible modal period' — the clarifying question is then asked without a suggested default rather than with a made-up one.
field_definitions.prior_strength: weak | calibrated. 'weak' means illustrative; 'calibrated' means fitted to a real population. Nothing in this file is 'calibrated' — the field exists so an institution replacing these values can mark which ones it has actually fitted, and so the audit log can distinguish the two.
field_definitions.source_detail: Free text: what the value is based on, or an explicit statement that it is not based on anything.
field_definitions.last_reviewed: ISO date this entry was last looked at. A prior nobody has reviewed in two years is a stale number with a provenance stamp, which is worse than an obviously undated one.
field_definitions.notes: Why this particular period was chosen as the illustrative default, and what would make it wrong.

insurance.source_detail: Not derived from any dataset. Chosen because motor and home policies in Ireland are commonly offered both as an annual lump and as a monthly/quarterly instalment plan, so no single period is safe to assume.
insurance.notes: This is the motivating case for the whole of Section 3. If a real distribution ever becomes available it should replace this first, because insurance is both high-value and genuinely split across periods.

subscription.source_detail: Not derived from any dataset. Reflects the prevailing default billing cycle of consumer streaming/software services.
subscription.notes: Weakest-consequence prior in the file: subscriptions are usually immaterial by the 5%-of-income test, so they rarely reach the clarifying-question path at all.

school_fees.source_detail: Not derived from any dataset. Reflects the academic-year billing convention.
school_fees.notes: Termly billing is common enough that 'annual' should not be trusted; the point of asking is precisely that a termly payer and an annual payer look identical after one observation.

sip.source_detail: Not derived from any dataset. Systematic investment plans are conventionally set up as monthly standing orders.
sip.notes: Used by InvestmentAgent's contribution detection as well as BudgetAgent — see agents/investment_agent.py _detect_contributions().

pension.source_detail: Not derived from any dataset. Reflects payroll-deduction cadence.
pension.notes: An AVC lump sum near the tax deadline is annual and would be misread by this prior — which is why the prior can only phrase the question, not answer it.

membership.source_detail: Not derived from any dataset. Professional bodies and clubs commonly bill yearly.
membership.notes: Gym memberships are monthly and would be misread by this prior.

maintenance.source_detail: Not derived from any dataset. Management-company service charges are commonly billed monthly or annually depending on the development.
maintenance.notes: Genuinely bimodal. A weak prior here is close to useless, which is itself the honest position.

property_tax.source_detail: Not derived from any dataset. Irish Local Property Tax is assessed annually, though it can be paid by instalment.
property_tax.notes: The instalment option is exactly why this still needs asking rather than assuming.

estimated_tax.source_detail: Deliberately null. Preliminary/self-assessment tax payment patterns vary too much between PAYE, self-employed and proprietary-director customers for any single modal period to be defensible.
estimated_tax.notes: A null modal_period is a first-class value, not a gap: build_clarifying_question() then asks without a suggested default, which is the correct behaviour when no default is defensible.
